description: Capital Bikeshare, the bike-sharing system of the Washington, DC region, publishes data on its membership, ridership and trip histories from its first trip in 2010 to today. Monthly trip files give trip duration, start and end date and time, start and end station names and numbers, bike number and member type (registered or casual, with the pass types listed). Staff trips, trips to or from warehouse test stations and trips under 60 seconds are removed. The page also offers real-time system data in the General Bikeshare Feed Specification, the proposed expansion plan as a KML file from the system's periodic development surveys, and reports of its member surveys (2014 and 2016 among them). The site is run by Lyft. Coverage: the Capital Bikeshare region. Format and access: downloadable files and feeds without registration. Licence and cost: free under the Capital Bikeshare Data License Agreement. Caveats: membership categories changed over time (the 3-day pass replaced the 5-day pass in fall 2011), and survey reports are dated. It supports capacity planning, demand modelling and agent-based studies of bike sharing. It is the data behind the Capital Bikeshare rebalancing case study and relates to the GBFS specification and Citi Bike data in the catalogue.
